historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance midpoint growth over FY2025 actual revenue (management's own forward-looking figure is a better anchor here than any trailing CAGR, given the business is mid-transition)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue CAGR (5.1% over FY23-25, the only years with a clean revenue figure in core_metrics) is running well above EPS CAGR (-2.0% to -1.8%) and FCF CAGR (-0.7% 3yr) over the same/nearby windows. This is NOT a data error: it is the mix-shift story itself -- gross margin compressed from 60.4% (FY2023) to 58.9% (FY2025) to 55.8-56.1% (H1 2026) as revenue mix shifts toward lower-margin cloud compute, and SBC as % of revenue rose from 8.6% (FY2023) to 12.7% (H1 2026) on AI/cloud headcount and LayerX integration -- so revenue growth is not converting to profit growth at the historical rate. The forward build explicitly does NOT extrapolate historical FCF margins; see assumptions.base for the component path.
historical_growth.notes: 5yr revenue CAGR is null because core_metrics/metrics_normalized only carries a clean Revenue figure from FY2023 onward for this ticker (older years show '-' in the normalized pivot); only the FY2023-FY2025 (2yr no annual figure prior) window is sourced. FCF CAGRs above are on REPORTED FCF, not owner FCF, because a consistent owner-FCF series requires interest-income and SBC-basis data only reliably available from FY2023 onward; the SBC and interest-income adjustments are nonetheless fully applied to the single FY2025 anchor used for last_fcf and to the forward build.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 guided growth (6.6%) accelerating to a management-guided 'low-teens' pace in FY2027-28 as the Anthropic and other 2026 AI-infrastructure commitments ramp, then decelerating to a 3% terminal rate; EBITDA margin dips through the FY2026-27 investment phase before recovering toward 33% as CIS contracts reach guided full-utilization economics; capex tapers from the guided ~40%-of-revenue FY2026 level toward a 10% steady state as the initial buildout completes. Owner FCF is negative for four years and matures to a ~12.7% margin -- below AKAM's historical peak but consistent with a structurally more capital-intensive, lower-gross-margin cloud/AI mix.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Anthropic relationship and adjacent frontier-AI-lab/enterprise deals scale toward and beyond the disclosed ~$20B potential; utilization ramps faster than guided so CIS hits its 60-70% gross-margin economics sooner and capex efficiency improves with scale; Security keeps compounding at a mid-teens clip. Terminal owner-FCF margin recovers to ~14.8%, back near Akamai's historical character despite the mix shift.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI capex supercycle funding this deal cools, or Anthropic/another counterparty pulls back; CIS utilization lags the capacity built for it and ~$5.5B of contractually-committed Anthropic-linked capex becomes semi-stranded; Delivery's structural decline continues unoffset. Owner FCF stays negative for six of ten years and matures to only a ~5.5% margin -- value-destroying capital allocation, though the legacy security/delivery business keeps the company solvent (terminal FCF stays barely positive, no zero-floor hit).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Akamai is mid-transition from a mature, high-margin CDN/security compounder into a much more capital-intensive AI/cloud-compute infrastructure provider, funded almost entirely by convertible debt and equity dilution (warrants) rather than internal cash flow. The Sept 24, 2026 Anthropic expansion (up to $11.6B, potential $20B) is the single largest disclosed catalyst in the company's history but is one day old at this valuation date -- it is deliberately NOT baked into base-case FY2026 growth (management itself says minimal FY2026 revenue impact) and only partially credited in FY2027-28 acceleration via management's own 'low-teens' commentary; the full bull-case scale of the relationship is treated as upside, not the central case. The capex step-up (~40% of revenue guided for FY2026, ~$5.5B tied specifically to Anthropic) is taken at face value and drives genuinely negative owner FCF for years 1-4 across all three scenarios -- this is not a modeling artifact, it is what the guidance says will happen, and ignoring it would materially overstate near-term intrinsic value. Net debt is calculated against total liquid assets (cash + short + long-term marketable securities, $4.6B) rather than cash alone, because the May-2026 $3.5B raise sits predominantly in marketable securities on the balance sheet.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI capex cycle sensitivity -- Akamai's entire forward growth acceleration is now levered to continued large-scale spending by a small number of frontier AI labs; any slowdown, renegotiation, or financing stress at Anthropic (or peers) directly hits the model's growth and margin recovery assumptions
Execution risk in an unproven, lower-margin, capital-intensive business where Akamai is structurally disadvantaged versus hyperscalers on GPU/co-location/power purchasing power

Convertible-note dilution mechanics -- the 2033 Notes' market-price trigger was already met at Q2 2026 (conversion price $93.01, well below the $110.41 current price) and reclassified to current liabilities; while note hedges cap the economic dilution up to warrant strikes ($155-$283/share), a sustained rally past those strikes, or vesting of the undisclosed-terms ~5% Anthropic warrant, would dilute per-share value beyond what this model's flat 153.686M share count captures
Legacy Delivery revenue (~30% of FY2025 revenue) remains in structural decline with no sign of stabilization, a permanent headwind the base case does not assume reverses

Gross margin compression from the cloud/compute mix shift (60.4% FY2023 -> 55.8-56.1% H1 2026) is a real, ongoing structural change, not a one-off -- the component build reflects it rather than extrapolating historical margins forward

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 70.82-165.45
data_sources.financials: research/AKAM/Reports/AKAM_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL + hand-filled recent-period revenue/gross-profit/debt, see AKAM_Corrections.jsonl); Q2 2026 10-Q and FY2025 10-K (research/AKAM/Extracted/) for balance-sheet anchors, interest income/expense, diluted share reconciliation and convertible-note terms not carried in core_metrics
data_sources.qualitative: research/AKAM/Reports/AKAM_Analysis.json (2026-09-25), including the recent_developments and guidance sections covering the Sept 24, 2026 Anthropic expansion

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement (Stock-based compensation add-back, $459.402M); 10-Q footnote 'Total stock-based compensation' reconciles to the same figure -- no separate equity-award-tax line disclosed, so no double-count risk
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% base: US risk-free ~4.2% + levered beta ~1.15-1.25 (moderate-cyclicality enterprise IT/security business now carrying a large debt-funded AI-capex bet) x ~5% ERP, plus recognition that convertible-note principal roughly doubled to $7.64B in May 2026. Bull 9.0% (de-risked once CIS contracts are proven and utilization ramps); bear 11.0% (leverage plus AI-capex-cycle and customer-concentration risk actually biting) -- risk charged once, in the cash flows and a modest WACC differential, not stacked on top of an already-conservative bear case.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (~$1.78B liability at Q2 2026) left OUT of net debt and out of the FCF build, consistent with standard US owner-FCF treatment for this business -- lease expense is already inside opex/EBITDA via rent, and leases are not the dominant capital structure item (converts are). Not adjusted per section 7 (US, non-cyclical-industrial routing; adaptations file not required).
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no minority interests on the balance sheet
inputs.notes: Routed via SKILL.md to the owner-FCF DCF, component-built (mature, profitable US operating tech company: CDN/security/cloud). 10-year explicit horizon used because FY2026-FY2029 owner-FCF margins are deeply negative-to-breakeven on the guided ~40%-of-revenue AI/cloud capex ramp and do not mature until roughly year 8-10 -- a 5-year horizon would capitalize an immature (negative) margin and badly understate the company. Net debt uses convertible-note carrying value ($7,562.828M, Q2 2026 10-Q) less CASH + SHORT-TERM + LONG-TERM MARKETABLE SECURITIES ($4,616.305M total), not cash alone -- the May-2026 $3.5B raise sits mostly in marketable securities, not the cash line, and using cash alone would overstate net debt by ~$3.1B. Share count is the GAAP diluted weighted-average for Q2 2026 (153.686M: basic 144.660M + stock-award dilution 3.673M + if-converted effect of the convertible notes 5.353M), NOT the 143.717M cover-page basic count -- using basic would ignore real dilution from in-the-money converts. The ~56.3M warrant shares tied to the note-hedge/warrant package (strikes $155-$283/share, all above the current $110.41 price) were excluded from GAAP diluted EPS as anti-dilutive and are likewise excluded here; if the stock re-rates toward those strikes (or the undisclosed-terms Anthropic warrant, up to ~5% of shares, vests and is in the money) that dilution is a real but currently unquantifiable risk flagged in valuation_philosophy, not mechanically added to the share count. Interest income ($70.808M FY2025, 'Interest and marketable securities income, net') is stripped from FCF because net cash-like assets ($4.6B) exceed 1x the FCF base -- otherwise the pile is counted twice. The Sept 24, 2026 $11.6B (potential ~$20B) expanded Anthropic deal is one day old at valuation date: management says it has minimal FY2026 revenue impact, so it is NOT layered into the FY2026 base-case growth rate (which matches pre-deal guidance), but it IS the main reason base-case growth accelerates to 10-11.5% in years 2-3 (translating management's 'low-teens 2027' commentary plus the deal's stated ramp) rather than staying at Akamai's pre-pivot mid-single-digit trend. The full ~$20B/7-year bull-case scale of the deal, and further expansion beyond it, is treated as the BULL case differentiator, not pulled into base.

bear.narrative: The AI capex cycle that funds the Anthropic and other 2026 commitments cools or a counterparty (Anthropic or another frontier lab) pulls back / renegotiates -- a real risk the Analysis JSON flags as 'high severity' given Akamai's small scale and weak purchasing power versus hyperscalers for the GPUs, co-location and power the buildout depends on. CIS growth undershoots the 50% FY2026 floor in later years as utilization on the built-out capacity stays low (the 6-9 month lag between signing and revenue recognition management describes cuts both ways -- capacity gets built ahead of demand that doesn't fully show up), while the committed ~$5.5B of Anthropic-linked capex is contractually spent regardless, becoming semi-stranded. Legacy Delivery keeps its structural decline with no offset. Security growth decelerates toward high-single-digits as hyperscalers and point-vendors compete harder. Owner FCF stays negative for six of ten years and only reaches a ~5.5% margin at maturity -- the business survives on its legacy security/delivery cash generation (which does not go to zero) but the AI pivot returns well below its cost of capital for most of the explicit horizon. Terminal value does NOT hit the zero floor (year-10 owner FCF is modestly positive, $333.7M), so this is a value-destroying capital allocation decision, not a going-concern scenario.

base.narrative: Revenue grows at the FY2026 guidance midpoint (6.6%) then accelerates to 10-11.5% in FY2027-28 as the initial Anthropic ($1.8B) and expanded ($11.6B, potential $20B) commitments ramp per management's 'low-teens 2027' commentary, alongside continued double-digit Security growth and a stabilizing (still slightly declining) Delivery drag; growth then decelerates smoothly to a 3% terminal rate as the AI-capacity buildout matures and CIS growth normalizes off its current high base. EBITDA margin dips to 26% in FY2027 (heaviest capacity build-out/lowest utilization) before recovering toward a 33% mature level as CIS contracts hit the guided 60-70% gross margin / 20-30% operating margin at scale and Delivery's drag shrinks as a share of a larger, more profitable total. Capex, guided at ~40% of revenue for FY2026, tapers from 38% toward a 10% steady-state as the initial GPU/data-center buildout completes and spend shifts to maintenance capex plus organic growth capacity; D&A rises with a lag as the new asset base is placed in service (peaking ~21% of revenue in FY2028-29) then eases as capex intensity falls below revenue growth. SBC stays elevated (12.5%) near-term reflecting AI/cloud hiring and the LayerX/Fermyon integration, then glides down slowly as the business matures. Cash tax ramps from 15% (below-statutory, reflecting the $852M deferred tax asset balance) to a 21% statutory-consistent rate by year 5. The result: owner FCF is deeply negative in years 1-4 (-24% to -2% of revenue) exactly as the guided ~40%-of-revenue capex implies, crossing to positive around year 5, and maturing to a ~12.7% owner-FCF margin by year 10 -- below Akamai's pre-pivot legacy-CDN margins but consistent with a structurally lower-margin, more capital-intensive cloud/AI mix.

bull.narrative: The Anthropic relationship scales toward the full disclosed ~$20B potential and attracts further frontier-AI-lab and enterprise customers on similar terms (the $600M robotics deal and other 2026 commitments are the leading edge of a broader pattern, not one-offs); CIS growth compounds well above the 'at least 50%' FY2026 floor for several years, taking total company growth into the mid-to-high teens by FY2027-28. Utilization on the new capacity ramps faster than guided, so CIS contracts hit their 60-70% gross-margin / 20-30% operating-margin economics sooner, and capex per dollar of incremental revenue improves (capacity built for Anthropic/robotics is reused across a growing AI-customer base rather than single-purpose). Security keeps compounding at a mid-teens clip on API security and Zero Trust/microsegmentation cross-sell. Terminal margin matures near 36% EBITDA / ~14.8% owner-FCF -- back toward Akamai's historical high-margin character despite the mix shift, because scale economics in the compute business finally offset the lower unit margin.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the house default 15% to 25% because the risk is not generic cyclicality but a specific, large, one-day-old capital commitment: convertible-note principal doubled to $7.64B in four months, ~$5.5B of capex is tied to a single counterparty relationship (Anthropic, now also a shareholder via warrant) that the Analysis JSON itself rates 'high severity' concentration risk, and management's own commentary concedes Akamai lacks hyperscaler purchasing power for the GPUs/co-location/power the buildout depends on -- several things need to go right, not one. Bull weight (30%, below base) reflects that the deal is real and already contracted (not speculative), so meaningful upside is plausible, but the full ~$20B/beyond scale and faster-than-guided utilization are not the modal outcome one day after the announcement, before any ramp has actually been observed. Base carries the guided numbers plus management's own 'low-teens 2027' commentary, nothing more.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
